text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 3

Both you and the successful candidate are men, and so was the whole panel. There is no plausible route by which your sex disadvantaged you here — raising it would read as grasping and undermine your credible complaint.

Your real argument is much stronger: on the stated criteria you dominate the appointee (completed vs. unfinished PhD, six vs. two papers, four years' teaching). The question is whether "strong industry experience" was in the advertised criteria and how it was weighted. If it wasn't advertised, that's a serious procedural flaw.

Focus there. Send a written follow-up citing your original request, the date, and any statutory or institutional deadline for giving reasons, then escalate to the HR director or appeals body.
